body: ## Problem No way to visually distinguish "special" files such as executables and symlinked files in the directory viewer. ## Solution For the issue of symlinks and executables, we can either a) provide a recipe, b) make it builtin, or c) do nothing. Looking at a working implementation is the easiest way to see what' the right decision for each, so I preliminarily coded them up. 1. **Executable files**: There's no notion of an "executable highlight group". I thought `PreProc` would fit best, but doesn't even have a visually differentiable highlight in the default colorscheme. Net effect: executables look the same, use `PreProc` by default. Open to introducing a new highlight group (*cringes*) or using other builtins (`Special`?) 2. **Symlinks**: see the image below for how things look. Rendered as EOL extmarks with `Dimmed`. However, I imagine there are many ways that users will want to render their symlinks - providing a recipe seems a bit more appealing here. Tagged echasnovski and glepnir just for insights on UI and appropriate colorscheme groups. closes #41310

comment_regular_data.body:
The typical convention for executable files is to append a `*` after their name (`ls -F`). Instead of highlighting the entire line differently, we should just do that (as virtual text with an extmark, of course).

This PR should probably also label FIFO pipes, sockets, etc. with their common symbols as well, again using the conventions from `ls -F`.

See the updated screenshot for appended *

The idea of "respect ls -F" as the goal I don't entirely agree with - I think it should be: "whatever fits the design of dir.lua and precedent set by things like vim-dirvish and {canola,oil}.nvim" - which may NOT work perfectly.

Anyways, good to record this conversation in history.

obligatory @justinmk
Is the 'suffixes' option relevant here? For "sorting" it definitely is relevant, not sure about highlighting.

> To be honest, being able to match dir.lua colors to ls...

See what the  original creator of the issue said [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41310#issuecomment-5302528705) - this is already not what we do here. This is pushing me more in the direction of _recipes_ rather than a one-off solution. Then again, executables and symlinked files are the **only** "real" special file cases we have left, so a builtin solution would make sense. Further, the documentation as it stands gives the user enough context to know that they can truly "do whatever they want", imo.

Any particular preference on this builtin vs recipe, Olivia & Justin?

> To be honest, being able to match dir.lua colors to ls...

In theory we could integrate with `$LS_COLORS`, but I don't think that's worth the effort. And if we don't do that, it's not possible to match `ls`'s colors (nor do we have highlight groups that are available to be used anyway). I think adding single character virtual text suffixes like you've done is the right way to go.

> Then again, executables and symlinked files are the **only** "real" special file cases we have left

I'd like to handle the niche file kinds if this becomes built-in (sockets, pipes, devices).

> Any particular preference on this builtin vs recipe, Olivia & Justin?

If this doesn't become built-in I'm basically going to copy the entire thing into my config, if that's anything.
